description: Verify the Sender Hardware Address field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals the configured DIface-0 MAC — identifies the resolver back to peers (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
The sender_mac field of an ARP Request lets the receiving peer learn '<sender_ip, sender_mac>' into its own cache (per RFC 826 §2.3). DUT must place its own outgoing-interface MAC there, not a stale or zero value. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request and asserts the sender_mac.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back; cache miss forces an ARP Request.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode      == 1
      - sender_mac  == DIface-0 MAC (DUT outgoing iface)   ← key check
      - target_ip   == HOST-1-IP

[Pass condition]
The observed ARP Request's sender_mac matches the DUT's configured DIface-0 MAC.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_sender_hw — ARP Request seen but sender_mac differed from the iface MAC (suggests bridge/bond misrouting or all-zero placeholder)
• Fail_timeout — No DUT ARP Request observed within the window

verdicts.Pass: ARP Request sender_mac matched DIface-0 MAC — normal
verdicts.Fail_sender_hw: ARP Request emitted but sender_mac did not match DIface-0 MAC
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP Request observed within the window
